items.description: One row of the document's generators section: a stochastic source declared under a name, so that any number of WorldDraw sites may reference it (Source). Declaring a source once and referencing it is what makes an NPC-bark site and a loot site able to share one authored table while still drawing independent sequences — the source carries the shape, each site carries its own position.

name.description: The source's name, unique within the section, and the spelling a site's Source resolves against.

source.description: Which draw shape this source fires.

start.description: Markov only: the context every emission begins from. Must name a declared context.

bound.description: Markov only: the maximum tokens one emission may draw before refusing by name, 1..MaxEmissionBound. Left at DefaultBound by a numeric source.

contexts.description: Markov only: the declared contexts, at least one, uniquely keyed.

items.description: One named context of a WorldGenerator — the state the walk may be sitting in and the weighted alternatives it may pick while there. A context declaring NO alternatives is TERMINAL: reaching it ends the emission.

key.description: The stable context key, unique within the generator.

alternatives.description: The weighted alternatives out of this context, or empty for a terminal context.

items.description: One weighted alternative of a WorldGeneratorContext: the token it emits, its relative weight, and the context the walk moves into after it is picked. The authored Next is what makes this a real Markov process rather than a bag of independent draws — the context key is the process state, so an author folds exactly as much history into it as the chain needs.

token.description: The opaque game-authored token this alternative emits. The engine never interprets it; it is space-joined with the emission's other tokens and written into the target text cell. Bounded by MaxTokenLength.

weight.description: The alternative's positive relative weight. At least one alternative in a context must carry a non-zero weight.

next.description: The context the walk moves into after this alternative is picked. Must name a declared Key; naming a context that declares NO alternatives ends the emission (a terminal is a context with nothing to say, never a reserved token spelling).

multiplicity.description: How many units of this alternative one pass holds, at least one; null is one. Under WithReplacement a multiplicity only scales the weight; under an exhausting mode each unit is drawn once per pass. A context's units total at most MaxEntriesPerSet.

mode.description: Markov, weighted numeric and symmetry orbit: how the entries are consumed (see WorldGeneratorMode).

rangeMin.description: UniformRange only: the closed range's inclusive lower bound — both bounds present or neither. Raw-encoded per the destination site's CellKind (raw FixedQ4816 bits for a fixed site) — unlike a site row's own min/max, which a fixed row authors as decimal text, since a source is not bound to one site and cannot know the kind it will write.

rangeMax.description: UniformRange only: the inclusive upper bound, same encoding as RangeMin.

weighted.description: WeightedNumeric only: the weighted numeric outcomes, at least one, at least one carrying a non-zero weight; under an exhausting Mode each outcome contributes Multiplicity units to the pass.

items.description: One numeric outcome of a WeightedNumeric source: the raw value it writes and its relative weight — the numeric twin of WorldGeneratorAlternative, minus Token (nothing to join into text) and Next (a numeric draw is one terminal pick, never a walk).

value.description: The raw value this outcome writes on selection (a plain integer for Int, raw FixedQ4816 bits for Fixed).

weight.description: The outcome's relative weight, fed straight to Puck.Maths.WeightedSampler's exact ulong overload. At least one outcome must carry a non-zero weight.

multiplicity.description: How many units of this outcome one pass holds, at least one; null is one. Under WithReplacement a multiplicity only scales the weight; under an exhausting mode each unit is drawn once per pass, so an outcome that should come out twice per pass declares 2 rather than being authored twice. A source's units total at most MaxEntriesPerSet.

ring.description: SymmetryOrbit only: the ring, 0..7, whose thirty nodes are the units — exactly one of Ring and Node.

node.description: SymmetryOrbit only: the node, 0..239, whose orbit under Word is the units.

word.description: SymmetryOrbit beside Node only: the word of reflections (one to eight mirror nodes, applied first to last) the orbit is taken under, or null for the lattice's own cycle — the same generator vocabulary a WorldStateCycle authors.
